step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows data ingestion from a customer environment into Splunk Cloud on AWS. Data sources include generic customer data, AWS Lambda, and Kinesis Data Firehose on the customer side. Standard HTTP Event Collector (HEC) data routes from the customer data source into a primary Elastic Load Balancer (Top ELB), while Kinesis Firehose routes through a dedicated Elastic Load Balancer (Bottom ELB) due to sticky session requirements. Both load balancers distribute traffic to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances representing Splunk indexers/search heads. Data is processed in EC2 cache tiers and then offloaded to Splunk S3 storage for primary persistence or archived into S3 Glacier. Splunk S3 also supports dynamic data self-storage export directly into the Customer S3 bucket.
